issues.legal_issue: A lease granted before the relevant cutoff is not subject to cancellation under the general power unless a specified ground for cancellation is established, and it is not automatically terminated by the later resettlement law.
material_facts: The claimant sought occupancy rights over land allotted to a displaced person and asserted that he or his forefathers had held the land from an earlier time.

The High Court held that the lease had been terminated under the resettlement law, without determining whether the claimant or a predecessor held a lease before the cutoff or in what capacity the land was held.
issues.conclusion: If the lease was granted before August 14, 1947, the Custodian could not cancel it unless satisfied that one of the grounds specified in the proviso to Section 12 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, applied; Section 9 of the Displaced Persons (Land Resettlement) Act, 1947, did not automatically cancel such a lease. Whether the claimant's lease met those conditions was left for the High Court to determine.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, permits cancellation or termination of leases of evacuee property, but its proviso restricts that power for leases granted before August 14, 1947, to cases involving subletting or parting with possession, use for a different purpose, or failure to pay rent. Section 9 of the Displaced Persons (Land Resettlement) Act, 1947, does not automatically terminate such a lease. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: challenge_to_lease_termination and lease_predates_cutoff and not (possession_parted_with or property_used_for_other_purpose or rent_not_paid)

predicates.challenge_to_lease_termination: A party challenges the termination of a lease over property subject to a statutory power of cancellation.
predicates.lease_predates_cutoff: The lease was granted before the cutoff to which the special protection for earlier leases applies.
predicates.possession_parted_with: The lessee sublet, assigned, or otherwise parted with possession of all or part of the leased property.
predicates.property_used_for_other_purpose: The lessee used the property for a purpose different from the purpose for which it was leased.
predicates.rent_not_paid: The lessee failed to pay rent in accordance with the lease.

issues.definition: When a challenged lease predates the relevant cutoff and none of the stated grounds is present, the lease is not automatically terminated or canceled.

issues.legal_issue: A writ petition cannot be dismissed on the basis that a lease was terminated without examining whether the claimant or a predecessor held a pre-cutoff lease and the resulting effect of the applicable statutory protections.
material_facts: The claimant asserted that he or his forefathers had been on the land from an earlier time and relied on revenue records concerning his grandfather's possession and the claimed inheritance of the lease.
The High Court did not investigate whether the claimant or a forefather held the land as a lessee before and through the relevant cutoff, or the capacity in which the land was held.
The High Court dismissed the writ petition by relying on the resettlement law, and its decision was affirmed on appeal within the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court judgments and remitted the matter for the High Court to determine whether the claimant or a forefather held the land as a lessee before and through August 14, 1947, and, if so, the effect of the applicable statutory provisions on continued possession and acquisition of occupancy rights.
issues.legal_principle: Where a claim to occupancy rights depends on whether a lease existed before the relevant cutoff and on the legal capacity in which land was held, the court must examine those factual matters before deciding the effect of the statutory protections. The Supreme Court relied on Section 12 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, and Section 9 of the Displaced Persons (Land Resettlement) Act, 1947. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.appeal_from_dismissal_of_writ_petition: The proceeding is an appeal from a decision dismissing a writ petition concerning a claimed lease or occupancy right.
predicates.claimant_asserts_pre_cutoff_lease: The claimant asserts that the claimant or a predecessor held the land under a lease before the relevant cutoff.
predicates.material_lease_facts_not_examined: The court that dismissed the petition did not determine whether the asserted lease existed or the capacity in which the land was held.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns dismissal of a writ petition, the claimant asserts a pre-cutoff lease, and material facts about that lease were not examined, the judgment is set aside and the case is remitted for factfinding.
